newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court rejects request for arrest of reporter.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court rejects request for arrest of reporter.

text.p: A Seoul court said on Tuesday it had rejected a request for an arrest warrant for a local journalist who reported that President Kim Young-sam's office secretly provided flour to North Korea.
State prosecutors had sought the permit to arrest Lee Kyo-kwan, 33, a reporter for the weekly magazine Sisa Journal, after Kim's chief secretary sued him for defamation.
Defamation through publication is a criminal offence carrying a maximum penalty of seven years in jail in South Korea.
"There was no evidence to verify the truth of Lee's report. But it is also hard to believe his story had malicious intention," said Seoul district court judge Hong Ki-jong.
"He appears to have attempted to fullfil the public's right to know."
The judge said Lee was unlikely to flee and destroy envidence. Lee, who had been held by investigators for questioning, was released overnight.

Lee said in a recent report that the presidential Blue House secretly provided 5,000 tonnes of flour to North Korea this year in a bid to seek help from Pyongyang for co-hosting of the 2002 World Cup soccer games.
The chief presidential secretary, Kim Kwang-il, filed a suit last week, saying Lee's article was groundless and that it defamed the presidential office.
Red Cross officials have said North Korea faces a long-term problem in feeding itself after floods and heavy rains this year and last year destroyed part of its arable land.
Japan and South Korea are co-hosting the 2002 World Cup.
